headline: Low pairwise risk overall: both profiles are non-runnable, network-egress-none docs-only artifacts with no shared I/O surfaces, so interaction pathways are largely absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile is runnable, and both expose no I/O surfaces or shared channel. Agent A is an awesome-list repo and agent B is a course repo; there is no documented path for A’s content to be ingested by B as instructions. The interaction is therefore provably blocked by missing communication surfaces.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF B begins parsing A-authored files as instructions, the severity increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents non-runnable in the current deployment.
Do not add shared clipboard or shared workspace mounts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents report network_egress:none and touch no data classes, so there is no documented route for sensitive data to leave one agent and reach the other or a third party. Because neither profile shows a shared workspace or authenticated principal, leakage is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, reassess leakage.
IF either agent gains outbound network access, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled on both agents.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation if shared storage is later introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented: both profiles have empty io_surfaces and empty concurrency_model, and both are non-runnable. Without shared mutable resources, there is no plausible write conflict between A and B.
conditions: IF either agent is given write access to the same directory or database, reassess conflict.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or mutable state, conflict analysis changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current setup.
Do not grant shared filesystem write permissions.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if shared mutable resources are added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static repository listing NLP resources, not an agent that generates operational facts, and B is a course repository with no action-taking authority. With no runnable behavior or documented output-to-input pipeline, B cannot treat A’s output as authoritative in a harmful cascade.
conditions: IF A becomes a live content generator and B consumes its outputs automatically, reassess.
IF B is extended to execute actions from A-derived content, cascading error risk rises.
mitigations: Keep A as a static reference artifact.
Require manual review before any downstream use of A-derived content.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before B acts on external outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either profile. Both touch no data classes and are open-source, docs-only artifacts, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch between A and B.
conditions: IF either profile is assigned regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention policies are added and differ, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through either profile.
Document residency and retention policies before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
